claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. 

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the first one:

**Do you have any children that you're responsible for?** If yes, could you please tell me their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I do. I have a daughter named Alex who's 15 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Now I need to understand a bit more about your situation and Alex's circumstances.

**Does Alex normally live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, she lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to check a few more details about your situation.

**Are you (or your partner, if you have one) responsible for Alex? This means you're responsible for things like her care, upbringing, and financial support.**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm responsible for her. I take care of her and provide for her needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Let me ask you about your immigration and residence status:

**Are you currently living in the UK, and do you have the right to reside in the UK?** (For example, are you a UK citizen, or do you have settled status, or another immigration status that allows you to live here?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK and I'm a UK citizen.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you. Now I need to understand Alex's situation a bit better:

**Is Alex currently in full-time non-advanced education or training, or has she left full-time education?** (Non-advanced education means education up to and including A-levels or equivalent, not university degree level.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: She's still at school - doing her GCSEs at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for that information. Let me just check a few final details to complete the assessment.

**Is Alex currently in hospital or in local authority care for an extended period?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, she's not in hospital or in care.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for answering all my questions. Let me now read the official guidance to make a complete assessment of your eligibility.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for your patience. Based on all the information you've provided and the official guidance, I can now make an assessment of your eligibility.

**Good news! You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Based on the information you've provided:
- Alex is 15 years old (under 16)
- She lives with you at home
- You are responsible for her care and financial support
- You are a UK citizen living in the UK
- Alex is in full-time education (doing her GCSEs)
- She is not in hospital or care

You meet all the key requirements for Child Benefit. You can apply for Child Benefit if you haven't already done so.

**Important note:** If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may have to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge, but you can still claim Child Benefit.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
